AI for accessibility

Designing for as many senses as possible, and finding that the structure AI adds to media is the same structure accessibility has always asked for.

I like designing for as many senses as possible: operating a video with the keyboard alone, making sense of one with no sound, or making sense of one with no picture. Once a video has structure, can be read and can be asked, it becomes friendlier to screen readers, silent viewing, keyboard navigation, low-bandwidth connections, older users and people with cognitive differences. In the work this site is drawn from, accessibility was not a patch after launch. It was the foundation.

4 patterns

  1. Index by product

    Turn a long video into a table of contents organized by the products in it, so a shopper can jump to the one they care about and skip the rest.

  2. Index by question

    Organize a video by the questions a shopper actually has, not by the products or the creator's edit, and hand the video back to the viewer's own priorities.

  3. Make mistakes easy to catch

    Assume the AI will be wrong some of the time, and design so the shopper notices quickly and can push back with almost no effort.

  4. Structure is accessibility

    The structure AI adds to a video so it can be asked is the same structure that makes it work without sound, without pictures or without a mouse. Build it as the foundation, not a patch.
